apps/api/test/analytics/traffic.test.ts:317-330 verifies only that one cleanup leaves one of 501 expired rows; it does not exercise scheduled backlog continuation. docs/progress/2026-09-29-cda-runtime-setup.md:17 describes retry records as lasting two hours.
findings.first_evidence: apps/api/src/analytics/service.ts:60:     (SELECT rowid FROM traffic_event_dedup WHERE expires_at <= ? ORDER BY expires_at LIMIT 500)`,
findings.suggested_fix: Keep bounded deletion batches, but drain or enqueue continuation while expired rows remain, using a bounded execution budget and a continuation mechanism when that budget is exhausted. Add a focused scheduler/cleanup test with several batches proving backlog progress exceeds supported ingestion and aggregates remain intact.
findings.title: Sustained traffic outpaces retry-record expiry cleanup

evidence: apps/storefront/app/utils/traffic.ts:15-22: identity fetch and response.json() are awaited without an AbortSignal or deadline.
findings.suggested_fix: Give identity acquisition (including JSON body consumption) and each event attempt a finite AbortController deadline, clearing the timer in finally. A 10-second deadline is a defensible default for optional analytics. Let the existing catches release the queue and Web Lock after timeout, preserve the identical event ID/body for the existing bounded retry, and add a focused stalled-request test proving later visits can proceed.
findings.title: Bound traffic requests so one stall cannot stop collection

residual_risks: Expired event retention depends on traffic volume: cleanupTraffic deletes at most 500 expired records and the scheduled handler invokes it once every five minutes, giving a sustained drain capacity of 100 events/minute. Above that aggregate ingestion rate the expired backlog grows indefinitely. No expected production traffic volume was available to establish whether this is a current operational defect.

Hosted D1 latency and query resource consumption at the configured 500,000-bucket reporting boundary remain unverified. The source uses indexed window predicates, bounds source rows, and batches daily SQL without transferring UV identities, so this review found no demonstrated runtime performance defect at expected usage.
testing_gaps: The storefront browser test covers direct navigation and reload with mocked identity/event endpoints, but does not exercise client-side product navigation via router links. A focused SPA navigation case should verify that page:finish observes the matching catalog-product payload and emits one product event, including returning to a previously visited product.

Built-storefront traffic E2E intercepts both identity and event endpoints, while API tests invoke a standalone Hono collector with a supplied cookie and source header. These establish each side separately but do not verify real browser Secure cookie persistence through the storefront service-binding gateway. A small gateway-to-collector browser check would cover that specific integration boundary; no failure at that boundary was established by inspection.

apps/storefront/app/utils/traffic.ts:28-49 introduces expiry renewal and 401/403 identity invalidation, but apps/storefront/tests/traffic.test.ts exercises only a fresh successful ticket, one network retry, and identity network failure. Add fake-clock cases for a later route visit after ticket expiry and a rejected event followed by a later visit; assert renewal, no retry of the rejected event, and a fresh event ID. This proves that ordinary long-lived shopper sessions resume collection without repeatedly submitting a rejected ticket.

apps/admin/src/pages/dashboard/dashboard-page.tsx:254-268 has a separate traffic response generation guard, while dashboard.test.tsx:201-231 defers only revenue for its stale-response test. Defer an old fetchTrafficReport, change the range, resolve the new response, then resolve and reject the old request in separate cases; assert that current UV, PV chart and ranking remain present. Revenue's shared financial guard coverage does not exercise this independent success/error guard.

The cleanup test verifies one 500-row batch, but no sustained-ingestion operational check verifies that the five-minute scheduled cleanup keeps expired dedup backlog stable. The current schedule can remove at most 100 rows per minute; this is a capacity boundary to measure against real accepted traffic, rather than a proven near-term defect.

apps/admin/src/pages/dashboard/dashboard.test.tsx exercises late financial completion, but not the independent trafficRequest generation guard. Add a deferred traffic request, change the date preset, settle the newer traffic result, then settle or reject the older request and assert that the UV card, page-view chart, and traffic ranking retain the newer scope. The implementation has matching effect cleanup and request guards; this is a coverage gap, not a demonstrated defect.

apps/storefront/tests/traffic.test.ts awaits every visit sequentially. Add overlapping A -> B -> A visits while identity initialization or the first delivery is deferred, then release it and assert three distinct entry events in order with one identity initialization. This directly exercises the newly introduced pending queue and lastPath dedup interaction used by app:mounted/page:finish. Existing browser tests cover mount duplication and simultaneous tabs, but not rapid same-tab transitions.
